notes: Every mutation here reverses one of the three standing controls named in
HISTORY WORTH KEEPING: on the first pass, P3-M3 (remove the visibility
check) and P3-M4 (restore the page-spanning offset assumption) had NO gtest
killer at all -- every gtest drove PdfContentWriter directly and none
reached ImageReplacer::replace(). The DCA's primary standing control was
therefore unenforced by anything that runs offline. That gap is what
to close, and the expect_fail sets below are the evidence they did. A
mutation with no killer is information, not a bookkeeping gap.

FILTER TRAP, found by the sweep itself: the filter was 'Recomposite*', which does NOT match 'Arrangements/RecompositeArrangementTest....' -- a TEST_P's full name begins with the instantiation prefix. The class-level rows therefore never ran, and every mutation 'survived' them vacuously. That is the same shape as a mutation whose patch failed to apply: an absent oracle and a surviving mutant are indistinguishable from the outside. Filter is now 'Recomposite*:Arrangements/*'.

P3-M2 EXPECTATION WAS WRONG, not the guard: 'always prefer the smallest overlapping image' is behaviourally IDENTICAL to the real rule on every region tested, because non-overlapping images are already discarded and the candidate set had one member each time. It is now killed by ARegionMostlyOverThePhotoResolvesToThePhotoNotTheThumbnail, a region that overlaps both images and whose correct answer is the LARGER one.

P3-M3 RETARGETED. The control it reverses was REBUILT mid-phase: the first version compared the region as rendered before and after the write, and reported a successful edit as FAILED because one user edit drives five recomposite passes and the later ones are visually but not byte-idempotent. The replacement asks, before writing, whether the target is the image drawn on top at that region. The mutation now neutralises that. See DCA 0105, 'Prevention / standing control', which records both versions rather than only the one that survived.

P3-M5 EXPECTATION WAS UNDER-DECLARED, not a guard failure. Guessing the ambiguous dimension match can resolve to the TOPMOST of the two same-sized images, which makes the write visible -- so the occlusion fixture's second test, which expects a failure verdict, legitimately dies too. Both are now declared. Recorded because the sweep reported it as a discrepancy first, and a discrepancy that turns out to be the author's arithmetic is worth as much as one that turns out to be the product's.

P3-M6 added for the GitHub #266 partial fix: EnrichedAtlas now records the DPI of the render its glyphs were cropped from, and GlyphAtlasCompositor rescales by composite/atlas DPI. The identity and unrecorded-DPI cases are asserted too, because the ratio is 1.0 on every single-DPI page and a wrong scale there would be a product-wide regression rather than a mixed-DPI one.

P3-M7 added for GitHub #266's second cause: GlyphAtlas now refuses a crop whose peak alpha does not exceed 128, because isolateAlpha gives 128 to a pixel equidistant between text and background -- so a mask below that contains nothing predominantly text. The measured bad glyph peaked at 127. The mutation makes the predicate always-true, which is what the code did before.

P3-M7 EXPECTATION WAS OVER-DECLARED, not a guard failure. I expected it to kill EmptyAndNullMasksAreNotInk too. It does not, and cannot: the mutated line sits inside `if (a > peak)`, and for an all-transparent mask the first pixel has a == peak == 0, so the branch is never entered and the mutant is unreachable on that input. A null mask returns earlier still. The sweep reported it as a discrepancy and the discrepancy was mine -- the third time in this pipeline an expect_fail set was wrong rather than a control being weak.
